blocked.name: Kiidk'yaas (the Golden Spruce)
blocked.reason: Dead. This rare golden Sitka spruce on the Yakoun River, Haida Gwaii, was deliberately felled by Grant Hadwin on 20-21 January 1997 (deep cuts left it standing weakened, it fell in a wind two days later) and never regrew; the site is now a stump/memorial. Confirmed by en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiidk%27yaas and en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grant_Hadwin, both describing the 1997 felling as final. Hard rule: never publish a dead tree as a collectible. Note for a later pass: cloned saplings grown from cuttings/scions exist at a few BC locations (e.g. a planting near Port Clements and one at UBC Botanical Garden); a genuine, named, visitable living successor could be researched as a separate, different lead, but it is not this tree and was not chased here.

blocked.name: Hollow Tree
blocked.reason: Dead. A c.800-year-old western redcedar stump in Stanley Park, Vancouver, hollowed by fire long ago; it lost its crown and became a stump-only landmark decades ago, was slated for removal after a December 2006 windstorm, and was structurally saved in 2011 with a concrete foundation and concealed steel supports funded by ~$100,000 in private donations (reopened October 2011). It is a preserved dead stump/heritage structure, not a living tree. Confirmed by en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollow_Tree and globalnews.ca coverage of the 2011 reopening. Hard rule: never publish a dead tree as a collectible, however famous.
